DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)

The clinical picture of a newborn with respiratory distress, combined with the blood gas showing respiratory acidosis (high PaCO2, low pH) and the chest X-ray demonstrating a ground-glass appearance with air bronchograms, is diagnostic for Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome. This condition typically results from surfactant deficiency, often seen in premature infants.
